title: AND, OR, and NOT Boolean Operators
description: Combine compound boolean predicates, master operator precedence, avoid logic bugs, and inspect Bitmap Index Scans.

data.text: Complex filtering requires combining conditions using `AND`, `OR`, and `NOT`. In SQL, **`AND` takes precedence over `OR`**, which is one of the most common sources of logical bugs in SQL queries.

data.title: Why Parentheses are Critical
data.content: Demonstrating how operator precedence alters query semantics.
data.code:
-- ❌ BUG: Evaluates as: role = 'ADMIN' OR (role = 'MANAGER' AND department = 'FINANCE')
-- Result: Returns ALL Admins regardless of department!
SELECT * FROM employees 
WHERE role = 'ADMIN' OR role = 'MANAGER' AND department = 'FINANCE';

-- ✅ CORRECT: Explicit parentheses group the OR condition first
SELECT * FROM employees 
WHERE (role = 'ADMIN' OR role = 'MANAGER') AND department = 'FINANCE';

data.text: When filtering with `OR` on two separate indexed columns (`WHERE email = $1 OR phone = $2`), PostgreSQL builds in-memory bitmaps of matching physical page addresses for both indexes and performs a **BitmapOr** operation before fetching actual heap tuples.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always wrap `OR` expressions in explicit parentheses when combining with `AND`.
PostgreSQL uses Bitmap Index Scans to satisfy multi-column `OR` filters efficiently.
